relationship: A single linear scale factor changes corresponding lengths by that factor, areas by its square and volumes by its cube.

learnerLoop.action: Drag an edge, fill four unit squares, lift cube layers, reverse area and volume factors, and repair an unequal height.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Lengths, corresponding face area, and volume derive from k, k², and k²h. h = k for similarity.
learnerLoop.evidence: Actual unit tilings and cube layers precede the displayed powers; unequal dimensions remain visibly unequal.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Use the relationship for a reverse target, a counterexample, or a self-directed comparison.

invariants: Similar solids keep one common linear scale factor across corresponding edges.
Area and volume factors are respectively the square and cube of that factor.
safeAdaptations: Vary positive scale factors and prototype dimensions.
Adjust working support while preserving the linked length, area and volume representations.
nonGoals: Applying the linear scale factor directly to area or volume.

prompt.description: A visually identified current mission, with context connecting the previous experience to the next action.

model.description: Lengths, corresponding face area, and volume derive from k, k², and k²h. h = k for similarity.
model.visibility: Always visible; later controls are progressively disclosed.

working.description: Worked examples precede learner calculations. Explicit quantity keys connect source labels to formula operands, with matching highlights and a button-triggered trace. Hover, focus and tap explain each source and calculation.

evidence.description: Actual unit tilings and cube layers precede the displayed powers; unequal dimensions remain visibly unequal.
evidence.visibility: In-place feedback; readings only in relevant steps.

completion.description: Advances only after the current model-derived criterion.
completion.visibility: Guided steps; absent in the open experiment.

scale.domain: 0.5 to 3 guided; 0.5 to 5 in the experiment, in steps of 0.1.
scale.output: Edge, face grid, cube grid and factor labels.

height.description: Independent height factor h for the non-similar counterexample.
height.domain: 0.5 to 3 guided; 0.5 to 5 in the experiment.

modes.guided: Small ordered visual investigations, with model actions and in-place revision.
modes.experiment: Ungated experiment: compare views, separate layers, change height independently, scale to factor 5 with automatic framing, record readings, and solve reverse area/volume targets.

dependencies: Build two layers, four cubes each.
Calculate k = 3 from area factor 9 and set the model to match.
Calculate k = 3 from volume factor 27 and set the model to match.
Restore the height to match the two other edge ratios.
Ungated experiment: compare views, separate layers, change height independently, scale to factor 5 with automatic framing, record readings, and solve reverse area/volume targets.
implementation.completion: Every guided criterion is evaluated from actual model state. Continue never bypasses an unmet criterion. Restart returns to the first step; Back repeats a prior step.
limitations: One-unit reference cube; face area means one corresponding face, not total surface area.
Continuous positive factors include partial units; all three powers apply only when h = k.
